Reviewer recommends rejection: Nearly every claim checks out against the sources, but two items need fixing before publication. (1) The FAQ answer 'Die drei Gründer bestimmten Huang von Anfang an zum CEO' is wrong: Britannica says Malachowsky and Priem selected Huang, so change it to 'die beiden Mitgründer'. (2) The body says Fox Business reported the $5 trillion milestone 'am 30. Oktober', but the visible byline on the fetched Fox page says 'Published October 31, 2025'. Only the page metadata says 30 October. Drop the report date or correct it. Optional: say 'Direktor einer Sparte' to match Britannica's wording. After these edits it can be re-checked and approved.

claims.claim: Born 17 February 1963 in Tainan, Taiwan (person.json facts, summary, FAQ, body)
claims.note: Britannica gives 17 Feb 1963 and Tainan. CHM gives 1963 and Tainan.

claims.claim: Age 63 as of October 2026
claims.note: Calculated from the birth date. Correct on 2026-10-26. The Britannica cache shows 'age 61', which is a stale snapshot.

claims.claim: At nine he went to a boarding school in Kentucky and had to clean toilets every day
claims.note: Britannica confirms the toilets and Oneida Baptist Institute. CHM only confirms that he moved to the US at nine. Britannica says he was sent to an uncle in Tacoma at nine and to Oneida 'shortly thereafter'.

claims.claim: About 50 years later he led the first company to reach a $5 trillion market value
claims.note: Fox Business calls Nvidia the first company in history to reach $5 trillion. A past milestone, so not outdated.

claims.claim: Co-founded NVIDIA in 1993
claims.note: NVIDIA's timeline says it was founded on 5 April 1993.

claims.claim: Second son of a chemical engineer and a primary-school teacher
claims.note: Britannica confirms it. CHM does not mention the parents' jobs.

claims.claim: Family moved to Thailand when he was five. The parents did not want to stay there because of the Vietnam War. The father had a good impression of the US from a Carrier training programme. The mother taught the sons 10 English words a day.
claims.note: All details are in Britannica.

claims.claim: At nine he and his brother went to an uncle in Tacoma. The uncle enrolled them at Oneida Baptist Institute thinking it was an elite school. It was a religious reform school for 'difficult' boys. His brother worked on a tobacco farm. Both were bullied.
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: Two years later the parents arrived and the family settled near Portland. He played table tennis at Aloha High School with a national ranking and graduated in 1981.
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: BSEE from Oregon State in 1984. He met engineering student Lori Mills there and later married her.
claims.note: Matches Britannica. The marriage is reported by Britannica and is relevant to the story (the foundation).

claims.claim: AMD 1984 to 1985, then LSI Logic until 1993, rising to head of a division
claims.note: NVIDIA's bio gives AMD 1984-85 and LSI 1985-93. Britannica says he became 'director of a company division'. 'Leiter' is slightly looser than 'director' but acceptable.

claims.claim: Master's in electrical engineering at Stanford, earned while working (also FAQ: alongside his job at LSI Logic)
claims.note: NVIDIA lists the MSEE from Stanford. Britannica says he returned to school 'while working' after LSI. No year is claimed.

claims.claim: NVIDIA founded on 5 April 1993 by Huang, Malachowsky and Priem to bring 3D graphics to gaming and multimedia
claims.note: Matches the NVIDIA timeline.

claims.claim: The two co-founders were chip designers and chose him as CEO. Start-up capital was $40,000, followed soon by $20 million from venture capital. This carried the firm through the difficult early years.
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: FAQ: 'Die drei Gründer bestimmten Huang von Anfang an zum CEO'
claims.note: Britannica says Malachowsky and Priem selected Huang as CEO. Huang was one of the three founders, so he did not choose himself. Fix to: the two co-founders chose him as CEO. The body text already says this correctly.

claims.claim: Huang has been president, CEO and board member since the founding
claims.note: NVIDIA's bio says so. The page is a 2024 publication, and nothing found suggests a change.

claims.claim: IPO in 1999. He tattooed the logo on his left shoulder when the stock hit $100.
claims.note: Matches Britannica.

claims.claim: GeForce 256 launched in 1999, the first GPU according to the Computer History Museum. It combined transform, lighting and rendering.
claims.note: CHM says this. The article attributes the 'first GPU' claim to CHM, which is appropriate.

claims.claim: In 2001 NVIDIA introduced a programmable GPU under Huang, according to IEEE
claims.note: IEEE says 'a programmable GPU in 2001'. The framing 'next step' is the editor's own.

claims.claim: CUDA launched in 2006, letting GPUs be used for general computing. Universities and national labs built some of the fastest supercomputers with them.
claims.note: Matches the CHM profile and NVIDIA timeline.

claims.claim: In 2012 AlexNet ran on NVIDIA GPUs and the company then refocused on accelerated computing for AI. Most AI models now run on NVIDIA technology.
claims.note: CHM says this. The NVIDIA timeline confirms AlexNet in 2012.

claims.claim: RTX in 2018, the first GPU with real-time ray tracing according to NVIDIA
claims.note: Matches the NVIDIA timeline and is attributed to NVIDIA.

claims.claim: At the 2018 GTC in San Jose he said GPUs were 25 times faster than five years earlier, faster than Moore's law. The press called it 'Huang's law'.
claims.note: Matches Britannica.
